messages.subject: Boxplot (almost certainly an idiot question)
parts:
Apologies, but it's shame myself publicly or destroy my laptop time
and my laptop is worth more.

I'd like to summarise the distribution of correlation coefficients for
four groups of coefficients. In boxplot it's simply a case of

boxplot(data)

with a load of extra options to try and make the plot look less pig
ugly.

I'm working my way through the ggplot manual (tryiing to avoid jealous
glances at the plots) and help files and I can't quite get it to
work. I think it's the way that my data file is laid out; four
columns of coefficients with headers for each:

Group1 Group2 Group3 Group4
1 0.9 0.7 -0.9
etc

I need the groups along the x-axis and coefficient (which will be -1
to 1) along the y. I can't quite get the syntax right to be able to
do this using qplot.

I know there's a simple solution, but it's eluded me for most of the
day, can anyone help?

Thanks

Mike

The easiest way is to "melt" your data:

dfm <- melt(mydf, measured = c("group1", "group2", "group3", "group4"))
head(dfm)
qplot(variable, value, data = dfm, geom="boxplot")

Melt is a part of reshape, which you can learn more about at
http://had.co.nz/reshape

Regards,
